questions.question: A patient with a pet rat who plays with it and gets many scratches presents with fever, chills, and fatigue. Blood culture returns a pleomorphic, gram-negative, filamentous rod.
questions.question_raw: You are seeing a patient with a pet rat. He likes to play with his rat and gets lots of scratches. He presents now with fever, chills, and fatigue. He has a blood culture return showing a pleomorphic, gram-negative, filamentous rod.

parts.text: What is the syndrome, and two organisms that cause this syndrome (genus and species)?
What single antibiotic can you use to treat it?
What are two viruses you could acquire from rat excrement in Canada (specifically in Canada, so not Hantaan or Lassa fever)?

parts_raw.text: What is the syndrome and TWO organisms that cause this syndrome (genus AND species please)
What antibiotic (only 1) can you use to treat?
What are TWO viruses that you could get from rat excrement IN CANADA (specifically said in Canada so no Hantaan or Lassa fever for you)

questions.model_answer: a) Syndrome: rat-bite fever. Organisms: (1) Streptobacillus moniliformis; (2) Spirillum minus. b) Penicillin G (intravenous). c) (1) Lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV); (2) Seoul virus (a hantavirus present in North America). Both are acquired from rodent excreta/secretions in Canada.
questions.beyond_mandell: Rodent-associated viruses in Canada (LCMV, Seoul hantavirus) are from PHAC/CDC zoonoses sources, not this chapter.
